diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the data are well-conditioned and the classes are separable, convergence is fast.

issues.failure_explanation: Strict convexity does not imply existence of a minimizer, and the logistic ERM is only strictly convex when the data matrix has full column rank. For linearly separable classes (the very case the text describes as favourable) the empirical risk has infimum 0 that is not attained, so no minimizer exists; for rank-deficient data the minimizer is not unique.

failure_location.quote: This function is smooth and (strictly) \emph{convex}, and therefore its minimization admits a unique minimizer.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses (full column rank, non-separable data) under which a unique minimizer exists, and remove or reword the separable-data remark.
issues.overall_effect: The stated structural property of the logistic-regression example is false in the separable and rank-deficient cases, contradicting the accompanying remark that separable data are easy.
issues.title: Logistic regression ERM claimed to always admit a unique minimizer
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis correction fixes the claim; nothing else depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the stationarity condition sum_i gamma_i grad R_i(theta*(gamma)) = 0 with respect to gamma_j gives grad R_j(theta*) + H dtheta*/dgamma_j = 0 with H the Hessian of the inner objective, so dC/dgamma_j = -(grad C)^T H^{-1} grad_theta R_j(theta*). The displayed formula uses the Hessian nabla^2 R_j (a matrix, making the right-hand side a row vector rather than a scalar) and defines H as a gradient rather than a Hessian, so the formula as written is not a valid hypergradient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace nabla^2 R_j by nabla R_j and define H as the Hessian nabla^2_theta of the inner objective.
issues.overall_effect: The 'exact update for the loss weights' advertised in this paragraph is incorrect as stated.
issues.title: Hypergradient formula for bilevel loss weighting is dimensionally wrong (Hessian instead of gradient of R_j; H defined as a gradient)
issues.why_classification: The correct formula follows from a one-line implicit-function computation; no downstream result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is well known that the GD iterates satisfy the following classical contraction bound

issues.failure_explanation: For a quadratic with constant Hessian H and fixed step alpha, the exact contraction factor of GD on the iterates is max(|1-alpha lambda_min|, |1-alpha lambda_max|), which equals (kappa-1)/(kappa+1) only for the optimal alpha = 2/(lambda_min+lambda_max). For any other alpha in (0, 2/lambda_max) the factor is strictly larger (e.g. for small alpha it is 1 - alpha lambda_min, close to 1), so the displayed inequality is false for the stated range of step sizes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound with the factor max(|1-alpha lambda_min|,|1-alpha lambda_max|), or restrict to the optimal step size.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed bound is incorrect as stated, although the qualitative conclusion (slow progress when lambda_min is small) still holds with the correct factor.
issues.title: GD contraction factor (kappa-1)/(kappa+1) asserted for every step size in (0, 2/lambda_max)
issues.why_classification: A standard local correction preserves the intended conclusion; nothing depends on the exact constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Taking full expectation and  using a variance transfer (see \cite[lemma 4.20]{garrigos2023handbook})  gives the main recursion:

issues.failure_explanation: The step claiming to follow 'from the definition of strong convexity' bounds alpha^2 E_k||grad f_{i_k}(theta_k)||^2 by alpha^2 sigma^2, but E_k||grad f_{i_k}||^2 = ||grad f(theta_k)||^2 + sigma^2(theta_k), so this bound is not implied by Assumption hp_noise (it also drops the factor ||theta_k-theta*||^2 on (1-alpha mu)). The following line then introduces the variance-transfer terms 2 alpha^2 sigma^2 + 2 alpha(2 alpha L_max - 1)(f - f*) as if derived from the previous one, which they are not; the correct argument must bound E_k||grad f_{i_k}||^2 by 4L_max(f(theta_k)-f*) + 2 sigma^2 before using strong convexity. The final recursion is correct but the chain of inequalities presented does not establish it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the faulty intermediate inequality by the standard variance-transfer bound E_k||grad f_{i_k}||^2 <= 4L_max(f(theta_k)-f*) + 2 sigma^2 and then apply strong convexity, yielding the displayed recursion.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:added-1 as written is invalid at the second-to-last inequality; the theorem statement itself remains true.
issues.title: Invalid intermediate inequality in the proof of the strongly convex SGD theorem
issues.why_classification: The standard cited lemma repairs the argument locally; the statement, rate, and constants survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound minimizes over k a quantity E||grad f(bar theta_K)||^2 that does not depend on k, where bar theta_K is only defined (as a weighted average) in the previous theorem; a bound on the gradient at an averaged iterate is not what the nonconvex analysis delivers and is not generally true. The constant L_f (smoothness of f) is never defined or assumed, and Delta_f^star in the bound differs from the defined Delta_f. As written the statement is not a well-posed theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound for min_k E||grad f(theta_k)||^2, define L_f as the smoothness constant of f (L_f <= L_max under Assumption hp_smooth), and use a single symbol for Delta_f.
issues.overall_effect: The nonconvex convergence guarantee is ill-defined as stated and its literal reading (gradient at the averaged iterate) is unsupported.
issues.title: Nonconvex SGD theorem stated with undefined quantities (L_f, Delta_f^star) and gradient at an undefined averaged point inside a min over k
issues.why_classification: The standard statement is recoverable by local corrections; the rate and hypotheses are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem th:nonconvex yields min_k E||grad f||^2 = O(1/sqrt K), so K = O(eps^-2) gives squared norm O(eps), i.e. gradient norm O(sqrt eps). Driving the gradient norm itself below eps requires E||grad f||^2 <= eps^2, i.e. K = O(eps^-4). The prose claims a complexity that is the square root of what the theorem supports.

failure_location.quote: This means that we need $\pazocal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ iterations to drive the norm of the gradient below the tolerance $\epsilon$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to 'to drive the squared gradient norm below eps' or change the complexity to O(eps^-4) for the gradient norm.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sample/iteration complexity for reaching an eps-stationary point is overstated by a square.
issues.title: Iteration complexity misstated: O(eps^-2) iterations give squared gradient norm O(eps), not gradient norm below eps
issues.why_classification: A one-phrase correction aligns the prose with the theorem; no other result is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Most of these points lie in regions where $f(x)$ and $r(x)$ are small, resulting in Jacobians that are nearly collinear.

exhibits $\lambda_{\max}\approx 4.0$ and $\lambda_{\min}\approx 0.30$,
in turn reducing the condition number to $\kappa(\Theta_7)\!\approx\!13$.

issues.failure_explanation: With phi_1''=-2 and phi_2''=2-12x+12x^2, J(x) = [2, -2+12x-12x^2]^T, which is independent of f and r (the model is linear in theta), so the claimed link between small residual and near-collinear Jacobians is invalid. Direct computation gives Theta_5 = [[4, 0.08],[0.08, 0.647]] with eigenvalues ~4.00 and ~0.645 (kappa ~6.2), and Theta_7 = [[4, -0.486],[-0.486, 0.786]] with eigenvalues ~4.07 and ~0.71 (kappa ~5.7). The reported values (0.02, kappa~200 -> 0.30, kappa~13) do not follow from the stated definitions, and the actual improvement in conditioning is negligible, so the example does not illustrate the claimed sharp increase of lambda_min. The preceding Weyl argument also only gives lambda_i(Theta_{m+1}) >= (m/(m+1)) lambda_i(Theta_m) and does not imply any improvement of kappa.

failure_location.quote: has eigenvalues $\lambda_{\max}\approx 4.1$ and $\lambda_{\min}\approx 0.02$, yielding a condition number $\kappa(\Theta_5)\!\approx\!200$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redesign the example (different basis functions or collocation sets) so that the stated eigenvalues are actually attained, or recompute and report the correct (near-unchanged) numbers and weaken the surrounding claims accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The concrete evidence offered for 'adaptive sampling improves the conditioning of the empirical NTK/Hessian' is incorrect; the section's claim is left unsupported by its own example.
issues.title: Adaptive-sampling Poisson example: reported NTK eigenvalues/condition numbers are inconsistent with the stated surrogate and points
issues.why_classification: No local edit preserves the advertised illustration; a new example construction (or withdrawal of the illustrative claim) is required, though no formal theorem depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The secant pair (s_k, y_k) is computed and saved only inside the branch k > S, so for k <= S nothing is stored; at k = S+1 the algorithm discards (s_1, y_1), which was never saved, and Algorithm alg:bfgs_twoloop, which loops over pairs i = k-1,...,k-S, is invoked at every iteration on pairs that do not exist. The procedure is therefore ill-defined as written and never accumulates the S most recent pairs it is supposed to use.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Save (s_k, y_k) unconditionally at every iteration and only discard the oldest pair when more than S pairs are stored; run the two-loop recursion over the currently stored pairs.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:bfgs does not implement L-BFGS as described (limited memory of the S most recent secant pairs) and is not executable as stated.
issues.title: L-BFGS pseudocode never stores secant pairs for k <= S, so the two-loop recursion uses nonexistent pairs
issues.why_classification: Reordering two pseudocode lines restores the standard, correct procedure; no guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The gradient of f_i(theta) = ell(h_theta(M^{-1}x), y) with respect to theta is (d h_theta/d theta)(M^{-1}x)^T grad_h ell; the input transformation M^{-1} (a d x d matrix acting on x) enters only through the evaluation point and cannot be multiplied against the output-space gradient grad_z ell as displayed. The displayed formula mixes input, parameter and output dimensions and is not the gradient of the stated objective.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display with grad_theta f_i = (partial_theta h_theta(M^{-1}x))^T grad_h ell, and explain that M^{-1} affects the direction through the evaluation point (and through partial_x h if the transformation is learned).
issues.overall_effect: The formal justification given for how input transformations alter the search direction is incorrect; the qualitative claim survives.
issues.title: Gradient formula for data-space preconditioning is dimensionally inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A local correction of an expository formula; nothing depends on it.
